cover.sub: 5 niche things that will make you
cover.title: annoyingly good at e‑invoicing

inner.title: pdfs don't count
inner.body: since 1 jan 2025, german b2b e-invoices must meet en 16931, like xrechnung or zugferd. a plain pdf no longer counts, however nice it looks.
inner.label: nice pdf though

inner.title: connect once
inner.body: on peppol, one certified access point lets you reach any receiver on the network. every invoice gets validated before sending, so sloppy data never leaves.
inner.label: one plug

inner.title: belgium fines you
inner.body: belgium fines businesses that can't send and receive structured e-invoices €1,500, then €3,000, then €5,000. your client may also lose their vat deduction.
inner.label: €5,000 later

inner.title: €50 per invoice
inner.body: france's reform applies from 1 september 2026, with €50 per invoice not issued electronically. the yearly cap is €15,000, somehow the comforting part.
inner.label: capped, at least

inner.title: poland's grace ends
inner.body: poland's ksef went mandatory in 2026, but small invoicers got until year end. that grace ends 1 january 2027, eleven weeks away.
inner.label: eleven weeks
